Physics

Module: superdex.physics

Core physics APIs.

Engine Lifecycle

Initialize and shut down the engine, and inspect whether it is running.

initialize(num_worker_threads: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None

Initialize SuperDex Physics by creating the process-wide context.

Only one context is needed for the entire process. It can be used to load shapes and create any number of scenes. Call shutdown() to clean everything up when you are done.

Parameters:

num_worker_threads – The number of asynchronous worker threads to initialize, or zero for single-threaded execution. Negative values (for example, -1) let SuperDex Physics choose a default based on the CPU hardware. Positive values are clamped to the number of logical processors.

Note

Simulation performance does not necessarily improve by using more threads. For simple scenes, using a small number of threads, or even single-threaded execution, may be fastest.

Raises:

RuntimeError – If SuperDex Physics is already initialized.

is_initialized() → bool

Return whether SuperDex Physics is currently initialized.

shutdown() → None

Shut down SuperDex Physics by destroying the process-wide context.

Any remaining state is immediately destroyed, including all scenes, actors, and constraints. Registered dependent contexts are destroyed first.

Warning

Must be called on the same thread that called initialize().

Raises:

RuntimeError – If SuperDex Physics is not initialized.

Execution & Threading

Inspect worker capacity and choose worker-pool or single-threaded execution.

get_num_threads() → int

Return the number of worker threads available to execute asynchronous tasks.

Returns:

The configured worker-thread count (see superdex::CreateContext), or zero if single-threaded mode is enabled (see set_is_single_threaded()).

Note

Call on any thread.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ API, which is not available in Python: superdex::CreateContext.

See also

superdex::CreateContext, is_single_threaded()

is_single_threaded() → bool

Return true if running in single-threaded mode.

Returns true when the Mochi context was created with zero worker threads (see superdex::CreateContext) or when single-threaded mode has been explicitly enabled via set_is_single_threaded().

Returns:

True if running in single-threaded mode.

Note

Call on any thread.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ API, which is not available in Python: superdex::CreateContext.

See also

set_is_single_threaded(), superdex::CreateContext

set_is_single_threaded(is_single_threaded: bool) → None

Enable or disable single-threaded mode.

In single-threaded mode, each new task will be executed on the calling thread, even if other threads are available. This may hurt performance, but it is useful for debugging and batch simulation.

Enabling single-threaded mode does not, however, terminate tasks that are already running asynchronously. Such tasks will run to completion. For example, if you have an superdex::AsyncScene, it will continue to step asynchronously, but each step will do its work on that one thread.

Parameters:

is_single_threaded (bool) – True to enable single-threaded mode. False to disable.

Note

Call on any thread.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ API, which is not available in Python: superdex::AsyncScene.

See also

is_single_threaded()

Scene

Simulation scenes.

DEFAULT_GRAVITY

Default gravity acceleration in world frame [m/s²].

class Scene

Bases: object

Represents a simulation scene.

Note

Each scene manages the simulation of a series of actors.

Note

Actors from different scenes do not interact with each other.

Warning

Concurrent access to the scene and its actors and constraints is illegal.

cancel_callback(self: Scene, handle: CallbackHandle) → None

Cancel a previously registered callback.

Parameters:

handle (CallbackHandle) – CallbackHandle from register_pre_step_callback() or register_post_step_callback(). Must be owned by this scene.

Note

Invalid and already-cancelled handles are ignored.

See also

register_pre_step_callback(), register_post_step_callback()

capture_state(self: Scene) → StateHandle

Capture the simulation state that changes from step to step for later restoration.

Captured state includes actor solution, transforms, and velocities; current and previous constraint/controller targets; and external forces.

Returns:

StateHandle to be used with restore_state(). Call release_state() or release_all_states() when you’re done with it.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Warning

Not supported for scenes with ROM actors.

See also

restore_state(), release_state(), release_all_states(), capture_state_to_file(), capture_state_to_bytes()

capture_state_to_bytes(self: Scene, out_data: DynamicArrayUint8) → None

Capture simulation state to a binary byte buffer.

Captures the same simulation state as capture_state(), but writes the binary representation to caller-owned memory instead of storing it internally. This is useful for transferring state between processes or caching state outside the scene.

Parameters:

out_data (ArrayLikeUint8) – Output byte buffer. Capture data is appended to the buffer.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

On failure, the output buffer may contain a partial capture. Discard the buffer or truncate it to its original size before reuse.

Warning

Has the same capture restrictions as capture_state(), including no support for scenes with ROM actors.

Warning

The binary representation uses an internal capture format. It is intended only for compatible scenes with the same actors and constraints created in the same order and the same component layouts, using the same SuperDex Physics build. It is not a stable long-term serialization or asset interchange format.

See also

restore_state_from_bytes(), capture_state(), capture_state_to_file()

capture_state_to_file(self: Scene, file_path: str) → None

Captures a snapshot of the state of a Scene, similar to capture_state(), then writes the data to a JSON file for manual inspection.

Parameters:

file_path (str) – Path of the output file to write/overwrite (case sensitive on some filesystems).

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Warning

Not supported for scenes with ROM actors.

See also

capture_state()

enable_actor_contact_asymmetric(self: Scene, colliding: ActorHandle, collider: ActorHandle, enable: bool, include_nested_actors: IncludeNestedActors) → None

Enable or disable collision detection between two actors. Order matters: controls only the specified direction (colliding actor checking against collider actor).

Parameters:

  • colliding (ActorHandle) – Handle of the colliding actor.

  • collider (ActorHandle) – Handle of the collider actor.

  • enable (bool) – True to enable contact, false to disable it.

  • include_nested_actors (IncludeNestedActors | int) – Whether nested actors should be affected by this contact setting. With NO, only the exact handles are affected. With YES, parent actors with nested actors resolve to the parent plus nested actors. The setting is applied to every ordered pair in the cross-product of the two resolved handle sets; no pairs outside that cross-product are affected. If the resolved sets overlap, pairs in the overlap, including self-pairs, are affected.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Contact is enabled by default. You only need to call this method if you wish to disable (or re-enable) contact for a specific actor pair.

Note

Both layer-to-layer and actor-to-actor contact must be enabled for contact to occur.

Note

Contact between adjacent links is automatically disabled when an articulated or soft-skinned actor is created. A later actor-contact setting can override that automatic disable for any pair included in the resolved actor sets. In particular, enabling contact between a parent actor and itself with YES enables contact between that parent’s nested actors, including adjacent links, unless a later actor-contact setting disables those pairs again.

Note

Call twice with swapped arguments or use enable_actor_contact_symmetric() to affect collision checks in both directions.

See also

enable_actor_contact_symmetric(), enable_layer_contact_asymmetric()

enable_actor_contact_symmetric(self: Scene, actor_a: ActorHandle, actor_b: ActorHandle, enable: bool, include_nested_actors: IncludeNestedActors) → None

Equivalent to calling enable_actor_contact_asymmetric() with actor_a and actor_b in both orders using the same include_nested_actors.

Parameters:

  • actor_a (ActorHandle) – Handle of the first actor.

  • actor_b (ActorHandle) – Handle of the second actor.

  • enable (bool) – True to enable contact, false to disable it.

  • include_nested_actors (IncludeNestedActors | int) – Whether nested actors should be affected by this contact setting. See enable_actor_contact_asymmetric() for details.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

See also

enable_actor_contact_asymmetric(), enable_layer_contact_symmetric()

enable_layer_contact_asymmetric(self: Scene, layer_a: str, layer_b: str, enable: bool) → None

Enable or disable collision detection for an ordered pair of contact layer names. Order matters: controls only the specified direction (actors in layerA checking against actors in layerB).

Parameters:

  • layer_a (str) – Name of the layer of the “colliding” actor (the one checking for contact). Must be non-empty.

  • layer_b (str) – Name of the layer of the “collider” actor (the one with a ColliderType being tested). Must be non-empty.

  • enable (bool) – True to enable contact, false to disable it.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Contact is enabled by default. You only need to call this method if you wish to disable (or re-enable) contact for a specific layer pair.

Note

Both layer-to-layer and actor-to-actor contact must be enabled for contact to occur.

Note

Call twice with swapped arguments or use enable_layer_contact_symmetric() to affect collision checks in both directions.

Note

Calling this method with a layer name not previously seen in the scene registers it as a new contact layer, increasing get_num_contact_layers() and adding the name to enumerate_contact_layer_names().

See also

enable_layer_contact_symmetric(), enable_actor_contact_asymmetric(), is_layer_contact_enabled()

enable_layer_contact_symmetric(self: Scene, layer_a: str, layer_b: str, enable: bool) → None

Equivalent to calling enable_layer_contact_asymmetric() with layer_a and layer_b in both orders.

Parameters:

  • layer_a (str) – Name of the first contact layer. Must be non-empty.

  • layer_b (str) – Name of the second contact layer. Must be non-empty.

  • enable (bool) – True to enable contact, false to disable it.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

See also

enable_layer_contact_asymmetric(), enable_actor_contact_symmetric(), is_layer_contact_enabled()

restore_state(self: Scene, handle: StateHandle, release_immediately: bool) → None

Restore captured simulation state. Optionally release the StateHandle at the same time.

Parameters:

  • handle (StateHandle) – StateHandle from a successful call to capture_state().

  • release_immediately (bool) – If true, release the state handle immediately (as if release_state() were called), even if the restore fails.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

The StateHandle must have been captured from this Scene.

Note

The scene composition (actors, constraints) must be the same as when the state was captured.

Warning

Does not create or destroy actors or constraints, or restore shapes, materials, or scene parameters. Captured mutable state on existing actors, including static actor transforms, is restored; if topology or persistent configuration changes, simulation results may differ.

Warning

Restoration is not transactional. If restoration fails, the scene may be partially modified. Restore a known-good checkpoint or recreate the scene before continuing.

See also

capture_state(), release_state(), release_all_states(), restore_state_from_bytes()

Note

The capture and restore scenes must use the same SuperDex Physics build.

Note

The restore requirements from restore_state() apply, including scene composition (actors, constraints) being the same as when the state was captured.

Warning

Has the same restore scope and non-transactional failure behavior as restore_state().

See also

capture_state_to_bytes(), restore_state()

set_force_single_island(self: Scene, force_single_island: bool) → None

Enables/disables forcing all actors in the scene to be in a single simulation island.

An island is a group of actors and constraints that are solved together. Islands are managed automatically based on proximity and other factors. Islands can be solved in parallel, which can greatly improve the performance of the scene. However, if you suspect that island partitioning might be causing a problem, then you can use this function to force all actors in the scene to be simulated in a single island.

Parameters:

force_single_island (bool) – Whether to force all actors to be in a single simulation island.

Warning

Forcing single-island is a debugging feature. It will hurt performance.

See also

get_force_single_island()

step(self: Scene, time_step_sec: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex) → None

Advance the simulation of the Scene one step.

SuperDex Physics uses fully-implicit time integration, enabling substantially larger stable time steps than physics engines using explicit or semi-implicit methods, particularly for stiff systems. Fewer steps per simulated second often improve simulation performance and real-time factor.

Parameters:

time_step_sec (float) – Time step size [s]. Must be non-negative.

Note

Time steps of 10–25 ms (40–100 physics steps per simulated second) run robustly in most scenes, including complex contact-rich and deformable simulations. This is a practical starting range, not a guarantee. Smaller steps may still be required to resolve fast motion, accurately capture short-duration contact dynamics without excessive numerical dissipation, resolve dynamics associated with small geometric or discretization length scales, or improve nonlinear-solver convergence.

Note

It is OK to use a different time step each time.

Note

If the time step is zero, then the state of the simulation will not change, but pre-step and post-step callbacks will still be called, and queries will be updated.

Note

If the time step is negative or NaN, no step is taken and an error is logged.

See also

IntegrationMethod

Please call this periodically if you are not actively stepping the scene. If this function is never called and the scene is never stepped, then some debugger features will not work.

Must be called on the scene’s owning thread (like other Scene methods).

create_scene(name: str) → Scene

Create a new Scene.

A scene is a collection of actors and constraints, which can be stepped to advance the simulation. Each scene is independent. Actors from one scene cannot affect another scene.

You can create a new scene on any thread, but that scene must only be accessed from one thread at a time. All reads and writes to the scene must be synchronous and well ordered. However, if you have multiple scenes, then it is safe to step them concurrently.

Parameters:

name (str) – Name of the new scene (for debugging).

Returns:

Pointer to the new scene. Call destroy_scene() when done with it.

Note

Call on any thread.

See also

destroy_scene()

destroy_scene(scene: Scene) → None

Immediately destroy a scene and all its actors and constraints.

Parameters:

scene (Optional[Scene]) – Pointer to the scene to destroy.

Note

No-op if scene is None or unknown to this Mochi context.

Note

Call on any thread.

Note

Any remaining scenes will be cleaned up automatically when the Mochi context is destroyed.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ APIs, which are not available in Python: superdex::AsyncScene, superdex::Context::DestroyAsyncScene.

Warning

Do not dereference pointers to the scene, actors, constraints, etc. after this call.

Warning

If scene is owned by an superdex::AsyncScene, the call is a no-op (a warning is logged). Call superdex::Context::DestroyAsyncScene instead.

See also

create_scene(), superdex::Context::DestroyAsyncScene

class GridSdfParams

Bases: object

Parameters controlling the resolution of grid-based Signed Distance Fields (SDF).

A GridSdf represents the SDF to a closed surface mesh as a 3D grid where each vertex stores the signed distance to the surface mesh. The SDF grid resolution and bounds are controlled by these parameters.

property boundary_padding_dist

Additional distance (in meters) to expand the mesh’s axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) when determining the SDF grid bounds.

The SDF grid will cover the mesh’s AABB expanded by this distance in all directions. This ensures the SDF has valid distance values even slightly outside the mesh’s AABB.

Note

In practice, this value should be greater than the value returned by get_penalty_threshold_dist(). If the SDF did not have enough padding, then Mochi would have to use a less efficient algorithm for collision detection, but it would still work.

Note

When you load a model and bake a uniform scale value less than 1.0, the model’s pre-computed SDF will also be scaled, resulting in less absolute padding. The default padding value is larger than the default contact penalty threshold distance for this reason.

See also

GRID_SDF_DEFAULT_BOUNDARY_PADDING

property min_grid_resolution

The minimum grid resolution measured in number of voxels per axis.

Note

This may override the voxel count (and voxel size) computed using resolution_mode and resolution_delta.

property resolution_delta

The maximum voxel size will be resolution_delta times the reference measurement computed using resolution_mode.

Note

The actual voxel size may be smaller because the number of grid cells will be rounded up to an integer value and clamped to a minimum of min_grid_resolution.

Note

Increasing resolution_delta will result in larger voxels. Doing so will make it harder for the SDF to resolve fine details of the mesh, but it will save memory and improve SDF generation speed.

Note

Decreasing resolution_delta will improve the SDF’s ability to resolve fine details, but it will take more memory and more time to generate. This cost scales proportional to N^3. Use with care.

See also

resolution_mode

property resolution_mode

Defines the mesh feature used as reference measurement for computing the voxel size.

See also

resolution_delta

class GridSdfResolutionMode

Bases: object

The maximum voxel size for an SDF will be determined by one of these measurements scaled by resolution_delta.

Members:

LARGEST_AXISUse the largest dimension of the mesh’s axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) as

reference.

SMALLEST_AXIS : Use the smallest dimension of the mesh’s AABB as reference.

MEAN_AXIS : Use the average of all three AABB dimensions as reference.

LARGEST_EDGE : Use the largest edge length in the mesh as reference.

SMALLEST_EDGE : Use the smallest edge length in the mesh as reference.

MEAN_EDGE : Use the average edge length in the mesh as reference.

EXPLICITUse resolution_delta to set the maximum

voxel size in meters (no scaling based on the features of the mesh nor AABB).

COUNT : Total number of resolution modes.

enable_file_cache(enable: bool) → None

Enable or disable the file cache.

When enabled, shape memory will be preserved even after the ShapeHandle has been released. Subsequent requests for the same file (with the same baked-in scale and transform) will be fast because the data will already be loaded. This can be an important optimization, but beware that it could waste memory if it preserves shapes that are no longer needed.

Parameters:

enable (bool) – True to enable, false to disable the feature.

Note

Call on any thread.

Note

Disabling the cache (passing false) immediately releases all currently cached shapes, equivalent to calling clear_file_cache().

See also

is_file_cache_enabled(), clear_file_cache(), clear_file_from_cache()

Get a view of the shape’s main mesh data.

For tetrahedral mesh shapes, returns the volume mesh (4 nodes per element). For triangular mesh shapes, returns the surface mesh (3 nodes per element). For polyline shapes, returns the polyline mesh (2 nodes per element). For shapes without a main mesh, including implicit shapes such as spheres and planes, returns an empty view.

get_shape_surface_mesh(shape: ShapeHandle) → MeshDataView

Get a view of the shape’s surface mesh data.

Returns a triangle mesh (3 nodes per element) representing the shape’s surface. The coordinate array contains exactly the surface nodes referenced by the returned connectivity; nodes present in the underlying main mesh but not referenced by any surface triangle are omitted. Connectivity values are indices into this returned coordinate array. For shapes without a surface mesh, returns an empty view.

Parameters:

shape (ShapeHandle) – Handle to a valid shape.

Returns:

A non-owning view of the shape’s surface mesh data, or an empty view if the shape has no surface mesh.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

For triangular mesh shapes, this may differ from get_shape_mesh() if the main mesh contains unreferenced nodes. For tetrahedral mesh shapes, this is the boundary surface of the volume mesh, with non-boundary volume nodes omitted.

Note

Can be called on any thread.

Note

The returned view will be invalid after the shape handle has been released.

See also

MeshDataView, get_shape_mesh(), get_shape_visual_mesh(), get_surface_mesh()

get_shape_visual_mesh(shape: ShapeHandle) → MeshDataView

Get a view of the shape’s visual mesh data, including skinning data if available.

Returns a triangle mesh (3 nodes per element) intended for visual rendering. Coordinates and connectivity are returned in visual-mesh node-index space, including any visual mesh nodes not referenced by the visual connectivity. The mesh may include linear skinning data for deformation. For shapes without a visual mesh, returns an empty view.

Parameters:

shape (ShapeHandle) – Handle to a valid shape.

Returns:

A non-owning view of the shape’s visual mesh data, or an empty view if the shape has no visual mesh.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Can be called on any thread.

Note

The returned view will be invalid after the shape handle has been released.

Note

When linear visual-mesh skinning data is present, skinning indices refer to the node ordering returned by get_shape_mesh(), not to the compact surface-node ordering returned by get_shape_surface_mesh(). Rod visual mesh embeddings are nonlinear and are not exposed through this linear skinning field.

See also

MeshDataView, get_shape_mesh(), get_shape_surface_mesh(), get_visual_mesh()

True if the file cache is enabled, false otherwise.

  1. load_shape_from_bytes(file_data: Span[str], bake_scale: superdex.physics.Real3) -> superdex.physics.ShapeHandle

Load a shape from a file of supported format, where the file has already been loaded into memory, and baking in some scale.

Supported formats: JSON (.mochi.json) and HDF5 (.mochi.h5), auto-detected from header bytes. To load a surface mesh format (OBJ, PLY, OFF, STL) from memory, use the overload that takes an explicit MeshFileType.

Parameters:

  • file_data (ArrayLikeChar) – File contents as an in-memory byte array.

  • bake_scale (Real3Like) – Scale to bake into the shape or (1, 1, 1) for no change. Negative scale results in mirroring.

Returns:

A ShapeHandle that can be used to create actors.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

The shape remains in memory while referenced by any handle or actor. In the C API, you must release the shape explicitly by calling release_shape(). In C++ and Python, this is optional, since ShapeHandle cleanup is automatic.

Note

Some shape data cannot bake arbitrary non-uniform scale. Unsupported scale values are rejected.

Note

Precomputed grid SDF data is preserved only when bake_scale is uniform by absolute value. Non-uniform scale by absolute value discards the precomputed SDF. If an SDF collider later requires SDF data, SuperDex Physics regenerates it from the transformed mesh at runtime, which may be expensive.

Note

If the loaded model has element_frame_axes, bake_scale transforms those axes as normal directions using the inverse-transpose of the scale transform, then normalize them.

Note

Call on any thread.

See also

ShapeHandle, release_shape(), load_shape_from_file()

Actors

Runtime physical bodies.

class Actor

Bases: object

Represents a simulated body (actor) in a scene.

Note

Every body in the simulation is an actor.

Note

Actors always belong to exactly one scene.

Note

Actors can be static or dynamic.

Warning

Concurrent access to the actor or its scene is illegal.

add_articulated_delta_to_pose(self: Actor, pose: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex], delta_dofs: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex], out_pose: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Add a pose delta to a pose using joint-aware composition.

Parameters:

  • pose (ArrayLikeReal) – Base pose as joint DoFs. Must be of size get_num_dofs().

  • delta_dofs (ArrayLikeReal) – Pose delta to add. Must be of size get_num_dofs().

  • out_pose (ArrayLikeReal) – Output pose after adding deltaDofs. Must be of size get_num_dofs().

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only applicable to articulated actors.

Note

Deltas cannot be simply added to poses. This function uses joint information to correctly add the delta.

Note

Useful for adding time-stepped velocity to a reference pose.

Note

For 3D rotations, delta values are interpreted as Lie-algebra rotation-vector increments.

Note

For 3D rotations, angular velocity is not directly the time derivative of the rotation vector representation.

See also

compute_articulated_pose_delta(), get_articulated_pose(), get_articulated_pose_distance()

add_articulated_pose_controller(self: Actor, params: PoseControllerParams) → None

Add a pose controller to an articulated actor.

Parameters:

params (PoseControllerParams) – Parameters defining the pose controller.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only applicable to articulated actors.

Note

Only one pose controller is allowed per actor. Adding a second controller raises an error.

Note

The initial target pose and target velocity are set to the actor’s current pose and velocity.

Note

Empty tracking arrays are allowed. Default zero-gain parameters are used for any empty array.

See also

remove_articulated_pose_controller(), has_articulated_pose_controller()

add_boundary_condition_constrained_nodes_at_rest(self: Actor) → None

Fix the “constrained nodes” at their world-space reference positions.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft and shell actors, except nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

Boundary conditions can be cleared with clear_boundary_conditions().

Note

Applies to constrained nodes specified by the actor’s mesh. Has no effect if none are specified.

Note

Each target position is computed by transforming the node’s mesh reference coordinate by the actor’s root transform.

Note

This API adds to existing boundary conditions. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world() for behavior when a DoF has more than one entry.

Warning

If the actor’s mesh has constrained nodes, calling this repeatedly without clearing re-adds the same boundary conditions and grows the per-step cost without bound. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world().

See also

clear_boundary_conditions(), add_boundary_condition_constrained_nodes_at_rest_permanent(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world()

add_boundary_condition_constrained_nodes_at_rest_permanent(self: Actor) → None

Permanently fix the “constrained nodes” at their world-space reference positions.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft and shell actors, except nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

Same as add_boundary_condition_constrained_nodes_at_rest(), except boundary conditions cannot be cleared.

Note

See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent() for interaction with clearable entries later added to the same DoF.

Warning

If the actor’s mesh has constrained nodes, each call adds a permanent boundary condition for every constrained node. Call this at most once. Repeated calls create duplicates that cannot be removed and irreversibly grow the per-step cost. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent().

See also

add_boundary_condition_constrained_nodes_at_rest(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent()

add_boundary_condition_dofs_world(self: Actor, dof_indices: Span[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], dof_values_world: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Add boundary conditions to specified DoFs.

Parameters:

  • dof_indices (ArrayLikeInt) – DoF indices to constrain.

  • dof_values_world (ArrayLikeReal) – Target values in the actor-specific representations described below. Length must equal dof_indices.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Not supported for nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

For soft and shell actors, each node has 3 consecutive DoFs containing its target x, y, and z position [m] in the world frame. All 3 must be specified together. Consider add_boundary_condition_nodes_world() as a more convenient alternative.

Note

For rigid and articulated actors, the DoF indices within each call must be sorted in strictly increasing order (no duplicate indices).

Note

Rigid actors have 6 DoFs: indices 0-2 are the target world-space center-of-mass position [m], and indices 3-5 are the target world-from-local orientation as a rotation vector (axis multiplied by angle [rad]). Either all or none of the 3 rotation DoFs must be specified.

Note

Articulated actors have a number of DoFs that depends on the number of joints and the DoFs per joint. When setting boundary conditions on the rotation of a free or spherical joint, either all or none of the 3 DoFs must be specified.

Note

Rod actors have 4 DoFs per node: the first 3 values are the target node x, y, and z position [m] in the world frame, followed by the next element’s scalar twist angle [rad]. (For open rods, the last DoF, i.e., the final node’s twist DoF, is included for padding only, does not affect the physics, and is automatically constrained to zero. This automatic constraint is not reported by get_boundary_condition_dof_indices(). For closed-loop rods, all twist DoFs are physical.) Boundary conditions on a rod node’s position must specify all 3 consecutive displacement DoFs for that node. Only zero values are allowed for the scalar twist angle in this function, with the interpretation that the element’s cross-section material axes rotate by only the minimal amount needed to remain orthogonal to the rod’s centerline. More elaborate control over rod element rotations should use constraints instead of boundary conditions.

Note

Boundary condition APIs add to existing boundary conditions; they do not replace existing entries. If a DoF has more than one entry, getter APIs return all entries in the order they were added, and the most recently added value is the effective value during the step.

Note

Boundary conditions can be cleared with clear_boundary_conditions().

Warning

Constrained 3D rotations may exhibit small numerical differences due to differences in the internal representation.

Warning

Adding a boundary condition to the same DoF more than once is legal — the most recently added value wins — but strongly discouraged. Each call adds an entry, so repeatedly re-adding without an intervening clear_boundary_conditions() grows the per-step cost without bound. To update a boundary condition, call clear_boundary_conditions() and add it again.

See also

clear_boundary_conditions(), add_boundary_condition_nodes_world(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent(), get_boundary_condition_dof_indices(), get_boundary_condition_dof_values_world()

add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent(self: Actor, dof_indices: Span[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], dof_values_world: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Add permanent boundary conditions to specified DoFs.

Parameters:

  • dof_indices (ArrayLikeInt) – DoF indices to constrain.

  • dof_values_world (ArrayLikeReal) – Target values in the actor-specific representations documented by add_boundary_condition_dofs_world(). Length must equal dof_indices.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Not supported for nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

Same as add_boundary_condition_dofs_world(), except boundary conditions cannot be cleared.

Note

If a clearable entry is later added for the same DoF, that clearable entry is the effective value until clear_boundary_conditions() removes it. The permanent entry is then the effective value again.

Warning

Permanent boundary conditions are retained for the lifetime of the actor and cannot be removed by clear_boundary_conditions(). Adding a permanent boundary condition to the same DoF more than once is legal but strongly discouraged. The duplicates can never be cleared and irreversibly grow the per-step cost. Add each permanent boundary condition only once.

See also

add_boundary_condition_dofs_world()

add_boundary_condition_nodes_world(self: Actor, node_indices: Span[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], node_positions_world: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Add world-space boundary conditions for specified nodes.

Parameters:

  • node_indices (ArrayLikeInt) – Node indices to constrain.

  • node_positions_world (ArrayLikeReal) – Target positions [m] in world frame. Length must be 3 times the size of node_indices.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft and shell actors, except nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

Boundary conditions can be cleared with clear_boundary_conditions().

Note

Equivalent to calling add_boundary_condition_dofs_world() with DoF indices (3*i, 3*i+1, 3*i+2) for each node i.

Note

This API adds to existing boundary conditions. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world() for behavior when a DoF has more than one entry.

Warning

Adding boundary conditions to the same nodes repeatedly without clearing grows the per-step cost without bound. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world().

See also

clear_boundary_conditions(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world(), add_boundary_condition_nodes_world_permanent(), get_boundary_condition_dof_indices(), get_boundary_condition_dof_values_world()

add_boundary_condition_nodes_world_permanent(self: Actor, node_indices: Span[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], node_positions_world: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Add permanent world-space boundary conditions for specified nodes.

Parameters:

  • node_indices (ArrayLikeInt) – Node indices to constrain.

  • node_positions_world (ArrayLikeReal) – Target positions [m] in world frame. Length must be 3 times the size of node_indices.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft and shell actors, except nested soft actors (see get_nested_soft_actors()).

Note

Not supported in differentiable scenes (make_scene_differentiable()) or for ROM actors.

Note

Same as add_boundary_condition_nodes_world(), except boundary conditions cannot be cleared.

Note

See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent() for interaction with clearable entries later added to the same DoF.

Warning

Add each permanent boundary condition only once. Duplicates can never be cleared and irreversibly grow the per-step cost. See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent().

See also

add_boundary_condition_nodes_world(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world_permanent()

handle (QueryHandle) – QueryHandle from register_query() or register_query_and_compute().

clear_boundary_conditions(self: Actor) → None

Remove all clearable boundary conditions previously added.

Note

Permanent entries are retained, but this call may change their positions in spans returned by get_boundary_condition_dof_indices() and get_boundary_condition_dof_values_world(). Do not cache those positions across this call.

get_articulated_controller_force(self: Actor) → Span[float]

Get the generalized forces applied by the pose controller on each joint DoF.

Returns:

Flattened generalized-force vector for each joint DoF. Size equals get_num_dofs(). Units are [N] for translational DoFs and [N·m] for rotational DoFs.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only applicable to articulated actors with a pose controller.

Note

Note

Requires the actor to support ARTICULATED_CONTROLLER_FORCE.

Note

Equivalent to using CONSTRAINT_FORCE on each of the pose controller’s constraints and projecting the constraint forces through the link Jacobians to joint DoF space (i.e., Σ Jᵢᵀ · fᵢ for each pose constraint i).

Note

If the solver diverged in the last simulation step, the returned generalized forces may be stale.

Get the limit values on all DoFs of the articulated actor.

Parameters:

out_dof_limits (ArrayLikeReal2) – Output span for DoF limits. Must be of size get_num_dofs().

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only applicable to articulated actors.

Note

Each element contains [min, max] limits for the corresponding DoF: [m] for translational DoFs and [rad] for rotational DoFs.

Note

Unconstrained DoFs have limits of ±infinity.

get_articulated_jacobian(self: Actor) → Span[float]

Get the Jacobian with respect to the articulated DoFs in world frame.

Returns:

Jacobian matrix in row-major order with shape [6, numArticulatedDoFs], where 6 is the number of rigid DoFs of the link (3 translation + 3 rotation) and numArticulatedDoFs is get_num_dofs() of the owning articulated actor.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only applicable to nested link actors within articulated actors.

Note

To get the Jacobian in the articulation’s root frame, left-multiply the Jacobian by the 6×6 block-diagonal of the root-from-world rotation:

[ R  0 ] · J
[ 0  R ]

where R is the 3×3 root-from-world rotation matrix (i.e., the transpose of the owning articulated actor’s world-from-root rotation).

See also

is_nested_link_actor()

get_boundary_condition_dof_indices(self: Actor) → Span[int]

Get the DoF indices that are constrained by boundary conditions.

Returns:

Span of DoF indices with boundary conditions applied.

Note

See add_boundary_condition_dofs_world() for the DoF layout for each actor type.

Note

The returned span contains every boundary-condition entry added through the public boundary-condition functions that has not been cleared, in the order the entries were added, including repeated DoF indices. Permanent and clearable entries are both included and are not distinguishable. Boundary conditions applied automatically by the engine are not included.

Note

Adding boundary conditions or calling clear_boundary_conditions() may invalidate the returned span. Do not retain it across either operation. Permanent entries are retained when clear_boundary_conditions() is called, but their positions within subsequently returned spans may change. Do not cache those positions across a call to clear_boundary_conditions().

See also

get_boundary_condition_dof_values_world(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world()

Permanent entries are retained when clear_boundary_conditions() is called, but their positions within subsequently returned spans may change. Do not cache those positions across a call to clear_boundary_conditions().

See also

get_boundary_condition_dof_indices(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world()

get_mesh(self: Actor) → MeshDataView

Get a view of the actor’s reference simulation mesh.

For soft actors, returns the tetrahedral mesh. For shell actors, returns the triangle mesh. For rod actors, returns the polyline mesh. For articulated actors with a skin mesh, returns the skin mesh. For articulated actors without a skin mesh, returns an empty view. For soft-skinned actors, returns the blended skin mesh when one is present and an empty view otherwise. For rigid actors whose shape is a tetrahedral or triangular mesh, returns their surface simulation mesh. For rigid actors with an implicit shape, such as spheres and planes, returns an empty view.

Returns:

A non-owning view of the actor’s reference simulation mesh, or an empty view if the actor has no simulation mesh.

Note

The returned coordinates are reference positions in the actor’s local frame. They do not include deformation for deformable actors.

Note

For rigid actors with tetrahedral or triangular mesh shapes, returns the same compact surface view as get_surface_mesh(). For tetrahedral meshes this is the boundary surface. For triangular meshes, nodes not referenced by any surface triangle are omitted and remaining nodes may be reindexed. Use get_reference_shape() and get_shape_mesh() to retrieve the original authored shape mesh.

Note

The returned view remains valid until the actor is destroyed.

See also

MeshDataView, get_surface_mesh(), get_visual_mesh(), get_shape_mesh()

For actors with SDF collider, the reported distance is only correct inside the actor’s bounding box. Outside the bounding box, it is an upper bound based on the triangle inequality.

Note

This function is not supported for soft actors or for the experimental POINT_CLOUD.

get_reference_shape(self: Actor) → ShapeHandle

Get a new ShapeHandle referencing the same shape data used to create this actor.

The returned handle is a new reference to the same underlying shape data. It will have a different numeric value from the ShapeHandle originally used to create the actor. The new handle represents a new request to keep the shape data in memory — the shape will remain valid as long as any handle, actor, or file cache entry references it.

Returns:

A new ShapeHandle referencing the actor’s shape data.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

In C++ and Python, the returned ShapeHandle is reference-counted and releases its reference automatically when destroyed. In the C API, you must call release_shape() when done with the handle to avoid leaks.

See also

release_shape(), load_shape_from_file()

get_rigid_moment_of_inertia_local(self: Actor) → Real6

Get the moment of inertia tensor of the actor at the center of mass, aligned with the actor’s local reference system (root transform), and using negative tensor notation.

    [ixx, ixy, ixz]   [ +∫(y²+z²)dm, -∫(xy)dm,    -∫(xz)dm     ]
I = [ixy, iyy, iyz] = [ -∫(xy)dm,    +∫(x²+z²)dm, -∫(yz)dm     ]
    [ixz, iyz, izz]   [ -∫(xz)dm,    -∫(yz)dm,    +∫(x²+y²)dm  ]
Returns:

kg·m².

Return type:

Upper-right triangle in the form [ixx, ixy, ixz, iyy, iyz, izz]. Units

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for dynamic rigid actors.

get_surface_mesh(self: Actor) → MeshDataView

Get a view of the actor’s reference surface mesh.

Returns a compact triangle mesh for the actor’s surface. For volumetric simulation meshes, the surface is the boundary triangles. For triangular simulation meshes, the surface has the same triangle elements as the simulation mesh, but nodes not referenced by any surface triangle are omitted and remaining nodes may be reindexed. Returns an empty view if the actor does not have a surface mesh.

Returns:

A non-owning view of the actor’s reference surface mesh, or an empty view if the actor has no surface mesh.

Note

The returned coordinates are reference surface-mesh positions in the actor’s local frame. They do not include deformation for deformable actors.

Note

The returned mesh uses compact surface-node ordering. Connectivity indices refer to this ordering, which may differ from the node ordering returned by get_mesh(). Interior nodes and nodes not referenced by any surface triangle are excluded. Results from get_surface_mesh_node_positions_local() and get_surface_mesh_node_normals_local() use this same surface ordering.

Note

The returned view remains valid until the actor is destroyed.

See also

MeshDataView, get_mesh(), get_visual_mesh(), get_surface_mesh_node_positions_local(), get_surface_mesh_node_normals_local(), get_shape_surface_mesh()

Get the normal direction for each node of the surface mesh in the actor’s local frame.

Returns:

Span of normals (3 values per node) in the actor’s local frame, computed by normalizing the area-weighted sum of adjacent triangle normals. The returned node list contains exactly the nodes referenced by get_surface_mesh() and is 1-to-1 with get_surface_mesh_node_positions_local().

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Requires registering SURFACE_NODE_NORMALS before the simulation step. Results are available after the simulation step completes.

Note

Requires the actor to support SURFACE_NODE_NORMALS.

Note

The node ordering corresponds to the mesh connectivity from get_surface_mesh().

See also

register_query(), SURFACE_NODE_NORMALS, get_surface_mesh(), get_surface_mesh_node_positions_local()

Returns:

Current node positions [m] of the surface mesh in the actor’s local frame (3 values per node: x, y, z). The returned node list contains exactly the nodes referenced by get_surface_mesh() and is 1-to-1 with get_surface_mesh_node_normals_local().

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Note

Requires the actor to support SURFACE_NODE_POSITIONS.

Note

The node ordering corresponds to the mesh connectivity from get_surface_mesh().

See also

register_query(), SURFACE_NODE_POSITIONS, get_surface_mesh(), get_surface_mesh_node_normals_local()

get_visual_mesh(self: Actor) → MeshDataView

Get a view of the actor’s reference visual mesh.

Returns a triangle mesh intended for visual rendering. The mesh may include linear visual-mesh skinning data when available. Returns an empty view if the actor does not have a visual mesh.

Returns:

A non-owning view of the actor’s reference visual mesh, or an empty view if the actor has no visual mesh.

Note

The returned coordinates are reference visual-mesh positions in the actor’s local frame. They do not include deformation for deformable actors.

Note

Includes visual mesh nodes not referenced by any visual triangle. Unlike surface mesh getters, visual mesh getters do not omit unreferenced nodes.

Note

When linear visual-mesh skinning data is present, skinning indices refer to the node ordering returned by get_mesh(), not to the compact surface-node ordering returned by get_surface_mesh(). Rod visual mesh embeddings are nonlinear and are not exposed through this linear skinning field.

Note

The returned view remains valid until the actor is destroyed.

See also

nx, ny, nz) in the actor’s local frame. The number of nodes is available via get_visual_mesh(). The order of the nodes is 1-to-1 with get_visual_mesh_node_positions_local(). Normals for visual nodes not referenced by any visual triangle are zero.

Flattened normals (3 values per node

Overloaded function.

  1. query_nodes_in_volume_local(self: superdex.physics.Actor, volume: superdex.physics.Aabb, boundary_only: bool, callback: collections.abc.Callable[[typing.SupportsInt | typing.SupportsIndex, superdex.physics.Real3], None]) -> None

Find the actor’s nodes that are inside an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB).

Parameters:

  • volume (Aabb) – Axis-aligned bounding box in the actor’s local frame.

  • boundary_only (bool) – If true, only boundary nodes are considered.

  • callback (Callable[[int, Real3], None]) – Callback called for each node found. The position is the current node position [m] in the actor’s local frame. The node index uses get_mesh() ordering, including when boundary_only is true.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

When boundary_only is false, this function supports only soft and shell actors. When true, it also supports articulated actors with a skin mesh, soft-skinned actors with a blended skin mesh, and rigid actors (dynamic or static) with tetrahedral or triangular mesh shapes. Rod actors and actors without a simulation mesh are not supported.

Note

Requires query registration before the simulation step. Register NODE_POSITIONS when boundary_only is false, or SURFACE_NODE_POSITIONS when boundary_only is true. Results are available after the simulation step completes.

Warning

This is a synchronous call and may be expensive.

register_query(self: Actor, type: QueryType) → QueryHandle

Register a query to compute data for this actor.

Parameters:

type (QueryType | int) – Type of query to register.

Returns:

QueryHandle for the registered query, or an invalid handle if registration fails.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Queries may add substantial computational overhead. Use only when necessary.

Note

Data is available after the next simulation step, even if its time step is zero.

Note

Call cancel_query() when the query is not needed again in the future.

Note

Queries are reference counted internally, so they will be available as long as there is one outstanding QueryHandle.

Note

Registration is all-or-nothing: if registration fails, no query is registered.

See also

cancel_query(), register_query_and_compute(), is_query_supported(), register_query()

register_query_and_compute(self: Actor, type: QueryType) → QueryHandle

Register a query for this actor and compute the result immediately.

Parameters:

type (QueryType | int) – Type of query to register.

Returns:

QueryHandle for the registered query.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Same as register_query(), except that the data is computed immediately (blocking) rather than at the next simulation step.

Note

Immediate computation is not supported for all query types. For unsupported types, the query is still registered successfully, immediate computation is skipped, and data becomes available after the next simulation step. See QueryType documentation for which types support immediate computation.

Note

Stepping the scene with zero time step is another way to force queries to update, without advancing the state of the simulation.

See also

register_query(), cancel_query()

External forces can be cleared with clear_external_forces().

Note

Replaces all previously set external forces, including external forces on DoFs not included in dof_indices. Passing empty dof_indices and force_values is equivalent to calling clear_external_forces().

Note

For rigid and shell actors, values are interpreted in the world frame.

Note

For articulated actors, values are generalized forces in the actor’s joint-DoF coordinate basis.

Note

For rod actors, forces on displacement DoFs are specified in the world frame, while (generalized) forces (scalar torques) on element twist-angle DoFs are always oriented along the corresponding element’s current orientation.

Note

For open (non-closed-loop) rod actors, the last DoF is padding that does not participate in physics, so it is invalid to apply a torque to it. For closed-loop rods, the last DoF is a physical twist angle.

See also

clear_external_forces(), get_external_forces(), add_boundary_condition_dofs_world()

set_inertia_properties(self: Actor, mass: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex, center_of_mass: Real3, moment_of_inertia: Real6) → None

Set the mass properties of the actor.

Directly sets mass, center of mass position in local coordinates, and moment of inertia tensor at the center of mass. This bypasses density-based computation and allows specifying exact inertia from CAD data or external measurements.

Parameters:

  • mass (float) – Mass [kg] to set. Must be positive and finite.

  • center_of_mass (Real3Like) – Position of center of mass [m] in actor’s local coordinate frame (get_root_transform()).

  • moment_of_inertia (Real6Like) – Moment of inertia tensor at center of mass [kg·m²], upper-right triangle [ixx, ixy, ixz, iyy, iyz, izz] using negative tensor notation consistent with get_rigid_moment_of_inertia_local(). Must be finite.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for dynamic rigid actors. Not supported for static actors, soft actors, shell actors, or articulated links.

Note

A finite but physically invalid moment of inertia tensor (negative principal moments or one violating the triangle inequality) is accepted with a warning, not rejected.

Note

Re-anchors the density reference state. Subsequent set_density() calls rescale mass and moment of inertia proportionally about the new values; center of mass is unchanged by set_density().

Note

After this call, get_density() returns bulk density mass / volume.

See also

get_mass(), get_density(), set_density(), get_rigid_center_of_mass_local(), get_rigid_moment_of_inertia_local()

set_node_positions_local(self: Actor, positions_local: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Set the current position of each node (reference + displacements) in the actor’s local frame.

Parameters:

positions_local (ArrayLikeReal) – Node positions [m] to set (3 values per node: x, y, z) in the actor’s local frame.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft (not soft-skinned) and shell actors.

Note

Does not change node velocities.

Note

Resets multi-step time integrators, e.g. BDF2 falls back to backward Euler in the first time step after this method is called.

set_node_velocities_local(self: Actor, velocities_local: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex]) → None

Set the current velocity of each node in the actor’s local frame.

Parameters:

velocities_local (ArrayLikeReal) – Node velocities to set in the actor’s local frame.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft (not soft-skinned), shell and rod actors.

Note

For soft and shell actors: 3 values per node [m/s] — (vx, vy, vz).

Note

For rod actors: 4 values per node — (vx, vy, vz) in [m/s] plus a twist rate [rad/s].

Note

Resets multi-step time integrators, e.g. BDF2 falls back to backward Euler in the first time step after this method is called.

set_recentering_params(self: Actor, params: RecenteringParams) → None

Set the recentering parameters of the actor.

When enabled for a soft actor, the root transform automatically moves as the actor’s “rigid pivot” (typically near the center of mass) moves.

Parameters:

params (RecenteringParams) – Recentering parameters to set.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft actors (not soft-skinned).

See also

RecenteringParams, get_recentering_params()

set_root_transform(self: Actor, world_from_local: TransformRT) → None

Set the actor’s world-from-local transform (root transform).

Parameters:

world_from_local (TransformRT) – World-space transform to set.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Not allowed on articulated links.

Note

For a top-level articulated actor, the local frame is the articulation root frame, not the root link’s frame.

Note

For dynamic actors, it does not change velocity. For static actors, however, it changes velocity, because it is implicitly defined by the root transform in consecutive time steps. To cancel the velocity of a static actor, use set_velocity().

Note

Resets multi-step time integrators, e.g. BDF2 falls back to backward Euler in the first time step after this method is called.

set_soft_material_params(self: Actor, params: SoftMaterialParams) → None

Set the material parameters of a soft actor.

Parameters:

params (SoftMaterialParams) – Material parameters to set.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft actors.

Note

If the ELASTIC_ENERGY query is active, invalidates the elastic energy baseline. One simulation step must complete before get_elastic_energy() returns valid results.

See also

get_soft_material_params(), set_soft_material_params_field(), set_density()

set_velocity(self: Actor, linear_vel: Real3, angular_vel: Real3) → None

Set the world-frame linear and angular velocity of the actor at the center of mass.

Parameters:

  • linear_vel (Real3Like) – Linear velocity [m/s] of the center of mass in world frame.

  • angular_vel (Real3Like) – Angular velocity [rad/s] at the center of mass in world frame.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for rigid actors (except articulated links) and soft actors (except ROMs and soft-skinned actors).

Note

For static actors, it only supports setting zero velocity.

Note

For soft actors, the angular velocity must be zero.

Note

Resets multi-step time integrators, e.g. BDF2 falls back to backward Euler in the first time step after this method is called.

set_zero_displacements_and_velocities(self: Actor) → None

Set all local displacement and velocity DoFs to zero.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only supported for soft, soft-skinned, shell and rod actors.

Note

For soft-skinned actors, it zeroes the elastic deformation and velocity only. The skeleton-driven pose is unaffected.

Note

For rod actors, it zeroes both the translational displacement DoFs and the twist-angle DoFs.

Note

Resets multi-step time integrators, e.g. BDF2 falls back to backward Euler in the first time step after this method is called.

class ArticulatedActorParams

Bases: object

Parameters to create an articulated actor.

Articulated actors are composed of rigid links connected by joints, forming a kinematic tree with optional cycle joints. Per-link properties are supplied via links, per-joint properties via joints, and cycle-closing joints via cycles. An optional skinned surface mesh can be attached via skin.

Contact is automatically disabled between links that are: (a) directly adjacent, (b) reachable via hard joints, or (c) reachable via (dummy) shapeless links. To enable or disable contact for specific pairs of links, see enable_actor_contact_symmetric().

See also

create_articulated_actor()

property cycles

Optional cycle joints creating closed kinematic loops. Empty if no cycles exist.

property joint_velocities

Optional initial joint velocity per DoF [m/s or rad/s].

See also

get_articulated_joint_velocities(), set_articulated_joint_velocities()

property joints

Joint parameters (one per joint).

Note

Size must match links.

property links

Link actor parameters (one per link). Must contain at least one link.

Note

Size must match joints.

Note

Links must be listed in parent-first order: the root link is at index 0 with parentLink == -1, and any other link’s parentLink must be smaller than its own index.

property name

Name of the articulated actor.

Note

Uniqueness of names is not enforced.

Note

Link actor names have the form “articulatedActorName/linkLocalName”, where linkLocalName is the link’s local name. If the articulated actor name is empty, link actors use “unnamed_articulation” as the parent name.

property skin

Optional skinned mesh parameters.

property world_from_root

Initial rotation and translation of the articulated actor’s local frame with respect to world frame.

property parent

class ArticulatedCycleJointParams

Bases: object

Parameters for a cycle-closing joint within an articulated actor.

Cycle joints close loops in the kinematic chain, enabling topologies beyond simple trees. Implemented as a soft spherical joint constraint (see joint_from_child_link and stiffness).

See also

cycles, ArticulatedCycleJoint

property child_link

Child link index.

property joint_from_child_link

Position and rotation of the cycle joint constraint in the child link’s local frame.

Note

A cycle joint is implemented using a spherical joint constraint. The joint_from_child_link translation defines the pivot point, in the child link’s local frame. Rotation is currently unused, but it could affect joint limits in the future.

property parent_link

Parent link index.

property stiffness

Stiffness [N/m] for the cycle joint constraint.

class ArticulatedJointFrictionParams

Bases: object

Per-joint friction parameters for articulated bodies.

Viscous and dry friction force/torque contributions are added together. - Viscous friction force/torque is proportional to velocity with coefficient viscous. - The static-friction peak/breakaway force/torque is given by coulomb + stiction_extra. Static friction is regularized to allow slight slippage at speeds of up to falloff_vel. - Above the smoothing threshold |v| > falloff_vel, dynamic dry friction force/torque (excluding additional viscous friction) has magnitude coulomb + stiction_extra * exp(-pow((|v| - falloff_vel) / stribeck_vel, 2)) when stribeck_vel is positive. If it is zero, the Stribeck term is omitted and the magnitude is coulomb. Here |v| is the magnitude of the relative (linear or angular) velocity. This causes friction to decrease smoothly from the peak static value to coulomb at high velocities.

property coulomb

Coulomb friction coefficient [N or N·m].

Note

Default is zero (no Coulomb friction).

property falloff_vel

Velocity threshold for dry friction smoothing [m/s or rad/s].

The dry friction force/torque smoothly transitions from 0 to the peak value as (linear or angular) velocity increases from 0 to falloff_vel.

Note

Smaller velocity thresholds improve physical accuracy but may degrade stability.

property stiction_extra

[Experimental] Extra stiction force/torque [N or N·m] representing the difference between static and dynamic friction.

Note

Must not be negative. The coulomb represents dynamic friction in the high-velocity limit, and peak static friction is coulomb + stiction_extra.

Note

Defaults to zero (no difference between static and dynamic friction).

Warning

This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at your own risk.

Warning

Nonzero values may harm convergence.

Warning

Nonzero extra stiction with zero Stribeck velocity results in a nonsmooth force.

property stribeck_vel

[Experimental] Stribeck velocity [m/s or rad/s] governing how sharply friction transitions from static to dynamic coefficients as velocity increases.

Note

Must not be negative. A smaller value means a sharper transition.

Note

Defaults to zero.

Note

This has no effect if stiction_extra is zero.

Warning

This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at your own risk.

Warning

Nonzero values may harm convergence.

Warning

Nonzero extra stiction with zero Stribeck velocity results in a nonsmooth force.

property viscous

Viscous friction coefficient [N·s/m or N·m·s/rad].

Note

Default is zero (no viscous friction).

class ArticulatedJointParams

Bases: object

Parameters describing a single joint within an articulated actor.

Each joint connects a link to its parent in the kinematic tree. Joints are referenced positionally — the i-th entry of joints corresponds to the joint connecting the i-th link to its parent. Cycle-closing joints are declared separately via cycles.

See also

ArticulatedActorParams, ArticulatedLinkParams, ArticulatedJointType

property axis

Local axis of motion for the joint, in the joint’s local frame.

Note

Only used for PRISMATIC and REVOLUTE joints. Ignored (and reset to zero) for other joint types.

Note

For Prismatic/Revolute joints, must be non-zero and finite. The vector is automatically normalized to unit length on actor creation.

property friction

Joint friction parameters.

Note

Ignored for FREE and HARD joints.

property inertia

Joint inertia coefficient. Units are [kg] for translation DoFs and [kg·m²] for rotation DoFs.

Note

Default is zero joint inertia.

Note

Ignored for FREE and HARD joints.

property limit_damping

Damping coefficient [N·s/m or N·m·s/rad] for the joint limit constraints.

Note

Ignored for joints without limits.

property limit_stiffness

Stiffness coefficient [N/m or N·m/rad] for the joint limit constraints.

Note

Ignored for joints without limits.

property max_limit

Maximum joint limits for each DoF. Units are [m] for translation DoFs and [rad] for rotation DoFs.

For 1D joints, limits must be defined by multiplying the scalar max limits by the joint axis. For 3D joints, each component must define the limit along one of the axes of the joint.

Note

The definition of joint limits for spherical joints may be complex, and it may be easier to model them as 3 co-located revolute joints.

property min_limit

Minimum joint limits for each DoF. Units are [m] for translation DoFs and [rad] for rotation DoFs.

For 1D joints, limits must be defined by multiplying the scalar min limits by the joint axis. For 3D joints, each component must define the limit along one of the axes of the joint.

Note

The definition of joint limits for spherical joints may be complex, and it may be easier to model them as 3 co-located revolute joints.

property name

Joint name. Must be unique among joints of the same articulated actor.

Note

If left empty, a unique default name (e.g., “joint_0”, “joint_1”, …) is assigned automatically.

property parent_link_from_joint

Rotation and translation of the joint with respect to the parent link.

property type

Joint type.

Note

Default INVALID is a sentinel. The user must overwrite it.

Note

CYCLE is reserved for cycle-closing joints. Use cycles for cycle joints.

Note

Static links can be modeled using a HARD joint whose parent is either -1 or another static link.

class ArticulatedJointType

Bases: object

Types of joints in an articulated body.

Members:

FREE : 6-DoF joint with unconstrained relative motion between links.

PRISMATIC : 1-DoF translational joint along a single axis.

REVOLUTE : 1-DoF rotational joint around a single axis.

SPHERICAL : 3-DoF rotational ball-and-socket joint.

HARD : 0-DoF rigid weld joint with no relative motion between links.

CYCLE : Cycle-closing joint in a closed-loop articulated topology.

COUNT

INVALID

property name
class ArticulatedLinkParams

Bases: object

Parameters describing a single rigid link within an articulated actor.

Each link is a rigid body in the articulation’s kinematic tree. Mirrors RigidActorParams for the per-link rigid-body properties (shape, mass, inertia, contact), and adds tree-structure fields (parent_link, parent_joint_from_link). Pose and velocity at creation time come from the articulated body, not from per-link fields.

See also

ArticulatedActorParams, ArticulatedJointParams, RigidActorParams

property boundary_element_type

Finite element type for boundary discretization.

Note

Affects accuracy and performance of contact and boundary integrals.

property boundary_subsampling

Optional subsampling for boundary integrals such as contact.

Note

Reduces computational cost by using fewer sample points.

Note

For best performance, combine subsampling with boundary_element_type = P1Q1.

property center_of_mass

Position [m] of the center of mass in the link actor’s local frame.

Note

If not set, computed automatically from geometry.

Note

Usually combined with explicit momentOfInertia.

See also

moment_of_inertia

property collider_type

Collision detection geometry.

Note

Determines how OTHER actors detect contact with this actor. It does not affect how this actor detects contact with other actors.

property contact

Contact mechanics parameters.

property density

Uniform density [kg/m³] of the actor. Must be positive if provided.

Note

Specify either density or mass, but not both.

Note

If density is set, mass is computed automatically from volume (and vice versa).

Note

If neither is set, DEFAULT_DENSITY is used.

See also

mass

property has_gravity

If true, the link actor will be affected by gravity.

See also

set_gravity()

property layer

Contact layer name for filtering contacts between actors.

See also

enable_layer_contact_asymmetric(), enable_layer_contact_symmetric(), enable_actor_contact_asymmetric(), enable_actor_contact_symmetric()

property mass

Total mass [kg] of the actor. Must be positive if provided.

Note

Specify either mass or density, but not both.

Note

If mass is set, density is computed automatically from volume (and vice versa).

See also

density

property moment_of_inertia

Moment of inertia tensor [kg·m²] at the center of mass in the actor’s local frame.

Stored as [ixx, ixy, ixz, iyy, iyz, izz] using negative tensor notation:

    [ixx, ixy, ixz]   [ +∫(y²+z²)dm,  -∫(xy)dm,    -∫(xz)dm    ]
I = [ixy, iyy, iyz] = [ -∫(xy)dm,     +∫(x²+z²)dm, -∫(yz)dm    ]
    [ixz, iyz, izz]   [ -∫(xz)dm,     -∫(yz)dm,    +∫(x²+y²)dm ]

Note

Uses negative tensor notation consistent with e.g. robotics URDF files.

Note

Many CAD tools (e.g., Solidworks) use positive tensor notation requiring negation of off-diagonal terms. See https://www.mathworks.com/help/sm/ug/specify-custom-inertia.html.

Note

Must be finite. A finite but physically invalid tensor (negative principal moments or one violating the triangle inequality) is accepted with a warning, not rejected.

Note

If not set, computed automatically from geometry and density.

Note

Usually combined with explicit centerOfMass.

See also

center_of_mass

property name

Link local name.

Note

Must be unique among links of the same articulated actor. For soft-skinned actors, it must also not collide with nested soft actor local names.

Note

Must not contain forward slash, backslash, or embedded NUL characters, which are reserved for hierarchy paths or incompatible with actor path formatting.

Note

If left empty, a unique default name (e.g., “link_0”, “link_1”, …) is assigned automatically.

Note

In the scene the corresponding actor is named “articulatedActorName/linkLocalName”. If the articulated actor name is empty, link actors use “unnamed_articulation/linkLocalName”.

property parent_joint_from_link

Rotation and translation of the link with respect to the parent joint.

Warning

The rotation must be identity. Non-identity rotations are not supported yet.

property parent_link

Index of the parent link in links, or -1 for the root.

Note

Links must be listed in parent-first order: parentLink < i for the i-th link.

Note

The root link (index 0) must have parentLink == -1.

property shape

Shape handle defining the actor’s geometry and other metadata.

Note

A shape can be shared by multiple actors, even actors in different scenes.

Note

Dynamic links require a shape with a surface mesh when link contact is enabled. An articulated actor enables link contact when no skin shape is provided. A soft-skinned actor enables link contact when enable_colliding_links is true.

See also

ShapeHandle, load_shape_from_file()

class ArticulatedShapeInfo

Bases: object

Information describing an articulated shape’s kinematic structure.

Provides read-only access to an articulated shape’s links, joints, and hierarchy. This information is immutable once the shape is created and defines the articulation’s topology and configuration limits.

Note

Number of joints = number of links + number of cycle joints.

See also

get_articulated_shape_info(), get_articulated_shape_info()

property cycles

Cycle joints creating closed kinematic loops in the articulated body.

Note

Empty if no cycles exist (i.e., the kinematic structure is purely tree-like).

Note

Cycle entries appear at indices [numLinks, numLinks + numCycles) of the per-joint arrays (joint_types, joint_axes, joint_from_child_link, parent_link_from_joint, joint_min_limits, joint_max_limits, joint_names).

See also

ArticulatedCycleJoint

property dof_info

DoF information of each joint (offset within the full pose, number of translation DoFs, number of rotation DoFs). Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

property joint_axes

Axis of each joint in the joint’s local frame. Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

property joint_from_child_link

Transform from each joint’s child link to the joint frame (rotation + translation). Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

This is the transform from the child link to the joint. parent_joint_from_link for tree joints and joint_from_child_link for cycle joints. The joint axis (joint_axes) and joint motion are interpreted in this joint frame.

property joint_max_limits

Maximum joint limits for each joint DoF. Size must be numLinks + numCycles, or empty if no joint has limits.

Limits are defined for either all joints or none. Joints without maximum limits are indicated by joint_max_limits[i] = superdex::kInf3. For 1D joints, limits are the scalar maximum limits multiplied by the joint axis. For 3D joints, each component defines the limit along one of the axes of the joint.

Note

The definition of joint limits for spherical joints may be complex, and it may be easier to model them as 3 co-located revolute joints.

Note

Size of joint_min_limits and joint_max_limits must be the same.

property joint_min_limits

Minimum joint limits for each joint DoF. Size must be numLinks + numCycles, or empty if no joint has limits.

Limits are defined for either all joints or none. Joints without minimum limits are indicated by joint_min_limits[i] = -superdex::kInf3. For 1D joints, limits are the scalar minimum limits multiplied by the joint axis. For 3D joints, each component defines the limit along one of the axes of the joint.

Note

The definition of joint limits for spherical joints may be complex, and it may be easier to model them as 3 co-located revolute joints.

Note

Size of joint_min_limits and joint_max_limits must be the same.

property joint_names

Name of each joint. Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

property joint_types

Type of each joint. Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

See also

ArticulatedJointType

property link_names

Name of each link.

property parent_link_from_joint

Joint frame of each joint expressed in its parent link’s local frame (rotation + translation). Size must be numLinks + numCycles.

This is the transform from the joint to the parent link, corresponding to parent_link_from_joint.

property parents

Parent link indices defining a tree-like joint structure with no cycles. Size must equal the number of links.

Note

parent[i] < i (parent must come before child in the array).

Note

Use -1 for links with no parent.

property root_from_links_at_rest

Rotation and translation of each link in rest configuration relative to the local reference system of the articulated shape. Size must equal the number of links.

class PoseControllerParams

Bases: object

Parameters to create a pose controller for an articulated actor.

Note

Each tracking array must be empty, have size 1, or have size equal to the number of links. Empty arrays use zero-gain defaults. Size-1 arrays are broadcast to all applicable constraints. Full-size arrays are indexed by link.

Note

Empty controllers are allowed. Constraints are created even when stiffness and damping are both zero, and can be accessed/updated via get_articulated_pose_constraints(), get_articulated_pose_controller_params() and set_articulated_pose_controller_params().

Note

Control of cycle joints is not supported.

See also

add_articulated_pose_controller(), PoseTrackingParams

Bases: object

Defines spring-damper parameters for individual pose tracking constraints in an articulated actor’s pose controller. Each constraint acts on a joint rotation, link translation, or link rotation.

See also

get_articulated_pose_controller_params(), set_articulated_pose_controller_params(), PoseControllerParams

property damping

Constraint damping.

Note

Units depend on the DoF kind: [N·s/m] for translation DoFs, [N·m·s/rad] for rotation DoFs.

Note

Must be non-negative and finite.

property saturation

Saturation distance [m] or angle [rad]. A negative value disables saturation.

Note

When enabled, saturation smoothly limits the magnitude of the elastic (stiffness) contribution to stiffness * saturation. The damping contribution is separate and is not limited by saturation.

Note

Must be finite and non-zero.

property stiffness

Constraint stiffness.

Note

Units depend on the DoF kind: [N/m] for translation DoFs, [N·m/rad] for rotation DoFs.

Note

Must be non-negative and finite.

class RecenteringParams

Bases: object

Parameters controlling recentering behavior for soft actors (not soft-skinned).

Recentering automatically updates the root transform as the actor’s “rigid pivot” (typically near the center of mass) moves, with corresponding adjustments to local-space coordinates.

Note

When recentering is disabled, local-space displacement values can become very large if the actor moves far from its starting position. This may be problematic due to finite-precision arithmetic.

Note

When recentering is enabled, the root transform rotates and translates to follow the actor, and local-space displacements reflect only deformation, not global rotation or translation.

See also

get_recentering_params(), set_recentering_params()

property rotation_epsilon_deg

Minimum rotation threshold [degrees] to apply recentering.

Note

Recentering is applied if either rotation or translation change more than their respective thresholds.

property translation_epsilon

Minimum translation threshold [m] to apply recentering.

Note

Recentering is applied if either rotation or translation change more than their respective thresholds.

property use_recentering

Whether recentering is enabled.

property moment_of_inertia

Moment of inertia tensor [kg·m²] at the center of mass in the actor’s local frame.

Stored as [ixx, ixy, ixz, iyy, iyz, izz] using negative tensor notation:

    [ixx, ixy, ixz]   [ +∫(y²+z²)dm,  -∫(xy)dm,    -∫(xz)dm    ]
I = [ixy, iyy, iyz] = [ -∫(xy)dm,     +∫(x²+z²)dm, -∫(yz)dm    ]
    [ixz, iyz, izz]   [ -∫(xz)dm,     -∫(yz)dm,    +∫(x²+y²)dm ]

Note

Uses negative tensor notation consistent with e.g. robotics URDF files.

Note

Many CAD tools (e.g., Solidworks) use positive tensor notation requiring negation of off-diagonal terms. See https://www.mathworks.com/help/sm/ug/specify-custom-inertia.html.

Note

Must be finite. A finite but physically invalid tensor (negative principal moments or one violating the triangle inequality) is accepted with a warning, not rejected.

Note

If not set, computed automatically from geometry and density.

Note

Usually combined with explicit centerOfMass.

See also

center_of_mass

property material

Uniform material properties.

Note

If the shape contains per-element material data of the same SoftMaterialType, the per-element values from the shape take precedence over and replace these uniform values. If the shape’s per-element material type differs, these uniform values are used instead.

Note

The actor uses a single PSD strategy for all elements. By default it is the material's PSD strategy. If the shape supplies per-element material data of a matching SoftMaterialType whose psd_strategy is specified (i.e. not MATERIAL_DEFAULT), that value takes precedence. If the material's PSD strategy is also specified, the two must be equal.

Note

Non-uniform material properties can also be applied after the actor is created. See experimental::SetSoftMaterialParamsField.

See also

set_soft_material_params(), set_soft_material_params_field()

property name

Optional actor name. Uniqueness of names is not enforced.
