property total_step_duration_sec

Total wall-clock time [s] spent in the last call to step().

Note

Includes time spent in user-defined pre-step and post-step callbacks.

enable_log_channel(channel: LogChannel, enable: bool) → None

Enable or disable log messages on the specified channel.

When a channel is disabled, messages on that channel are discarded before reaching the logging callback (see set_log_callback()).

Parameters:

  • channel (LogChannel | int) – The log channel to enable or disable.

  • enable (bool) – True to enable the channel, false to disable it.

Note

By default, all channels are enabled except for VERBOSE.

Note

Call on any thread.

See also

is_log_channel_enabled(), set_log_callback()

get_debug_server() → DebugServer

Get the debug server for this context.

Returns:

Reference to the DebugServer, which accepts connections from external debug tools.

See also

DebugServer

is_log_channel_enabled(channel: LogChannel) → bool

Return true if messages on the specified log channel are enabled.

Parameters:

channel (LogChannel | int) – The log channel to query.

Returns:

True if the channel is enabled, false otherwise.

Note

Call on any thread.

See also

enable_log_channel()

log(message: str, channel: superdex.physics.LogChannel = <LogChannel.INFO: 1>) → None
set_log_callback(callback: collections.abc.Callable[[LogChannel, str, str, SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], None]) → None

Optionally provide a callback function to redirect SuperDex Physics logging. The default function outputs to stdout and to the debugger (if attached).

Parameters:

callback (Callable[[LogChannel, str, str, int], None]) – Function to handle logging, or None to restore the default logging function.

Note

Call on any thread.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ API, which is not available in Python: superdex::Context::GetLogCallback.

Warning

Your callback function may be called on any thread.

See also

superdex::Context::GetLogCallback

class CoordinateSpaceAxes

Bases: object

Combination of axis directions for a coordinate space convention.

Each three-letter name gives the semantic direction of positive X, positive Y, and positive Z, respectively. For example, FLU means X-forward, Y-left, Z-up.

Members:

RUF : X-right, Y-up, Z-forward (Unity).

RUB : X-right, Y-up, Z-backward (OpenGL, Filament).

RDF : X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.

RDB : X-right, Y-down, Z-backward.

LUF : X-left, Y-up, Z-forward.

LUB : X-left, Y-up, Z-backward.

LDF : X-left, Y-down, Z-forward.

LBD : X-left, Y-backward, Z-down.

ULB : X-up, Y-left, Z-backward.

DLB : X-down, Y-left, Z-backward.

class RoutingElement

Bases: object

One ordered element in a spatial tendon’s heterogeneous routing list.

A WAYPOINT uses index (a link index) and local_position; a LINEAR_JOINT uses index (a joint index) and coefficient. Order matters: a segment forms only between adjacent waypoints, so a linear-joint element between two waypoints leaves a gap.

property coefficient

Signed constant moment arm d(displacement)/d(joint DoF) [m / joint DoF]. Only used for linear-joint elements. Its sign sets whether the tendon lengthens or shortens with the joint DoF.

property index

Link index for a waypoint, or joint index for a linear-joint element.

property local_position

Waypoint position in the link’s local frame, the same frame in which the link’s mesh and geometry are authored (the link’s root-transform frame) [m]. Only used for waypoint elements.

property type

Selects the interpretation of the remaining fields.

class RoutingElementType

Bases: object

Selects how a RoutingElement is interpreted by a spatial tendon.

Members:

WAYPOINTA point fixed in a link’s local frame. Adjacent waypoints are joined by a

straight segment whose length contributes to the tendon length.

LINEAR_JOINTA constant moment arm contributing coefficient * jointCoordinate. Carries no

geometry and breaks the polyline between waypoints.

property name
UNIT_INTERVAL

The unit interval [0, 1].
